causal_chain: The Educational Legacy Fund funded a new dry EEG for UAA’s AI and Robotics Lab; students and faculty have trained.
Its scalp sensors record electrical activity, allowing graduate student Vadim Egorov to observe his own signals and anticipate collecting recordings tailored to his research tasks.
UAA plans reading and programming studies; results are still ahead.
Researchers can use suitable existing public recordings or design new recordings around a different task.
Recordings require interpretation. Future models claiming to work for new people should be tested on people excluded from training; this is a general principle, not a reported UAA result.
